column1: # ================ *** BUT THE ONE URUGUAYAN HIT IS A REAL LEAD ON HER FAMILY *** ================
# Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, Montevideo, *** 15 MAY 1812 *** - ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-X7PG-M:
#   "bautice solemnemente a BONIFACIA AGUSTINA que nacio el dia catorce ... hija legitima de DON FELIX
#    MALBAREA y de DONA MICAELA FERNANDEZ, naturales de esta Ciudad. Abuelos Paternos Don Bernardo
#    Malbares y Dona Manuela Lozano: *** Abuelos Maternos DON RODRIGO FERNANDEZ Y TRESGUERRAS y DONA
#    ROSA FERNANDEZ. *** Fueron Padrinos DON JUAN AGUSTIN SERENA y DONA AGUSTINA PERENA."
# *** DON RODRIGO FERNANDEZ Y TRESGUERRAS IS THE FIRST PURCHASE THIS ARCHIVE HAS EVER HAD ON MARIA'S
# OWN FAMILY. *** A man of that exact compound surname, at Montevideo, with a daughter MICAELA of
# marriageable age by 1812. *** Maria Fernandez Tresguerras is very plausibly his daughter and Micaela's
# sister - and that is a PLAUSIBILITY, not a finding. *** No act read here says so.
# *** AND THE GODPARENTS ARE WRITTEN "SERENA" AND "PERENA". *** This archive has documented the machine's
# S-for-L on this family five times - Abelino Serena, Luis Serena, Avelino Serena, Levena, Sancio. So
# "Juan Agustin Serena y Agustina Perena" is very likely a LERENA couple standing at the font of a
# Fernandez y Tresguerras grandchild in 1812. *** If so, the two families were already joined - which is
# exactly what a marriage in 1791 would predict. ***
# *** SAID AGAINST MYSELF: *** Juan Agustin cannot be Sancho's son, who would be a child in 1812. He
# would be a brother, a cousin, or no relation at all - and "Serena" may simply be Serena. *** The
# reading is offered as the next thing to test, not as a result. *** The act to open is the 1812 image
# itself at full magnification, to see whether the hand wrote L or S.
# ================ *** LATER THE SAME DAY: THE DATE GETS A SOURCE, THE PLACE LOSES ONE *** ================
# FamilySearch blocked this session ("Access Denied - Error 15"), so the films could not be touched. Geneanet
# was open, and the jfina tree carries a sourced note that changes three things in the file above.
# 1. *** THE 8 JANUARY 1791 DATE IS NOT "WHAT THE TREES SAY". *** It descends from JUAN ALEJANDRO APOLANT,
#    "Operativo Patagonia" (Montevideo, Imprenta Letras, 1970), *** FICHA 355 *** - a named published work with
#    a numbered entry. Obtaining that page is now the cheapest route to whatever Apolant himself cited.
# 2. *** THE PLACE HAS NO SOURCE AT ALL, AND THIS FILE'S OWN TITLE ASSERTS IT. *** The note gives the date and
#    then "Consejo de Morcin, Asturias", which is the BRIDE'S ORIGIN - her own page reads "Born in 1778 -
#    Concello de Morcin. Asturias". *** "Canelones, 8 January 1791" welds a sourced date to an unsourced venue. ***
#    The venue is still the best inference going: the 1812 padron lists all six children as "naturales del
#    CANELON", the eldest aged 21 and so born about 1791. *** But it is an inference and this file said it flat. ***
# 3. *** THE "SAID AGAINST MYSELF" ABOVE IS WITHDRAWN - IT WAS BAD ARITHMETIC. *** It reads "Juan Agustin cannot
#    be Sancho's son, who would be a child in 1812." The 1812 padron gives *** JUAN AGUSTIN, 21 *** and
#    *** AGUSTINA, 17 *** in that household. Sancho's eldest son and eldest daughter, both adults, with exactly
#    the two forenames standing at that font. *** The archive talked itself out of a correct reading with an age
#    it never checked - and "SERENA"/"PERENA" is the machine's S-for-L for the sixth time. ***
# *** AND THE "PROBABLY NOT DIGITISED" VERDICT ABOVE IS OVERSTATED. *** It rests on a FULL-TEXT search, and full
# text covers only a fraction of what FamilySearch has filmed. Guadalupe de Canelones has marriage books from
# 1775, so the act exists. *** Whether its images are browsable has never been checked, and that - not full
# text - is the first thing to do when the block lifts. *** See data/apolant-ficha-355.tsv.
